articles.title: Apple, Samsung, and other phone makers don’t think they can sell as many phones in 2027
articles.excerpt: The smartphone market is bracing for troubled times ahead.
articles.body: TL;DR Most major phone makers have reportedly lowered their 2027 shipment targets due to rising memory costs. Xiaomi and vivo are cutting the most, by 25% and 29% respectively, while Apple and Samsung are also reducing their targets. HONOR is the only major phone brand that’s not reducing its shipment target for 2027. The memory shortage has been a theme throughout this year, and we’ve seen several manufacturers hike phone prices because of it. Now, it seems to be hitting manufacturers’ sales plans as well. According to a report from Jiemian News , citing supply chain sources, most major smartphone makers have finalized their shipment targets for 2027 and expect to sell considerably fewer phones next year.
articles.author: Akshay Gangwar

articles.title: The Godot MCP server installs cleanly. Then every run_project call fails on a headless box
articles.excerpt: You add the server the way its README says: claude mcp add godot \ -e GODOT_PATH=/usr/local/bin/godot \ -- npx @coding-solo/godot-mcp tools/list comes back with 14 tools. run_project answers like it w…
articles.body: You add the server the way its README says: claude mcp add godot \ -e GODOT_PATH = /usr/local/bin/godot \ -- npx @coding-solo/godot-mcp tools/list comes back with 14 tools. run_project answers like it worked: Godot project started in debug mode. Use get_debug_output to see output. Then get_debug_output answers, every single time: No active Godot process. No stack trace, no stderr, nothing in the client log. The project never started, and nothing in the response says why. The README does not cover this Its troubleshooting section has four entries: Godot Not Found , Connection Issues , Invalid Project Path , Build Issues . None of them is "the engine started and died". The word headless appears zero times in the README (I re-fetched main today to be sure).

articles.title: DaisyRose-27B vs Qwen3.8-27B: Mac benchmarks
articles.excerpt: RadixArk released DaisyRose-27B on 18 November 2026, a reinforcement-learning post-train of Qwen3.8-27B under Apache-2.0, and we ran it locally on a Mac through our two agentic coding benchmarks, whic…
articles.body: RadixArk released DaisyRose-27B on 18 November 2026, a reinforcement-learning post-train of Qwen3.8-27B under Apache-2.0, and we ran it locally on a Mac through our two agentic coding benchmarks, which score from 0 to 1. On Gauntlet its one run scored 0.6896, level with Gemini 4 Neon's one cloud run at 0.6658. Its two Forge 2.0 builds on the board scored 0.3322 and 0.3254, above the base's two October builds at 0.2576 and 0.1128. The base's only Gauntlet number is 0.0915. It comes from an October cloud run scored by an older version of our scorer, so I don't treat that gap as a before and after. If you want it on a Mac, the 8-bit weights take about 31 GiB of memory. On a 128 GiB M5 Max Mac Studio it decoded 24 to 27 tokens a second with prompts up to 40k tokens, peaking at 37.3 GiB.

articles.title: OpenCode vs Claude Code (2026): Cost, Models, and Trade-Offs
articles.excerpt: OpenCode vs Claude Code gets confusing fast—“OpenCode” is two things under one roof. One is a free, open-source coding agent (terminal, desktop, and mobile) that connects to models from 200+ providers…
articles.body: OpenCode vs Claude Code gets confusing fast—“OpenCode” is two things under one roof. One is a free, open-source coding agent (terminal, desktop, and mobile) that connects to models from 200+ providers. The other is OpenCode Go , a $10-a-month subscription covering 33 models. Claude Code is Anthropic’s closed-source agent, built around Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Haiku 5.5, and it starts at $20 a month on Claude Pro . OpenCode vs Claude Code: the short answer Pick Claude Code ($20 on Claude Pro) if you want Opus 5.5 or Sonnet 5.5. A subscription buys far more Opus than the same money spent at API rates , and your Pro login only works in Anthropic’s own apps. Pick OpenCode with OpenCode Go ($10) for model variety at half the entry price. You get a published limit for every model.

articles.body: TL;DR Gemini Notebook can now incorporate images from uploaded study materials into flashcards, making visual learning easier. You can now schedule flashcard review reminders through the Gemini mobile app, and all three improvements are available without a paid subscription. Google has been adding some interesting features to Gemini Notebook lately. Just a few days ago, we reported that the tool could turn your research materials into interactive websites. articles.body: Credit: Akshay Gangwar / Android Authority TL;DR Gemini’s floating overlay on Android now uses screen context to find the best shopping deals across apps. You can ask it to check if a product is worth considering or compare prices across different apps. The feature works by grabbing a screenshot of the page behind it but doesn’t require you to share your screen with Gemini Live. Google already curates products from multiple online stores in the Shopping section of its search results. If you’d rather skip manually scouring products, you can ask Gemini or Google’s AI Mode to recommend or filter them based on your preferences . Now, Google is making these insights even more accessible with prompts on top of any popular shopping app on your phone.

articles.excerpt: Finally, someone who texts you first and brings good news.
articles.body: TL;DR The latest Google Messages beta integrates Gemini Tasks through the app’s existing floating Gemini button. Gemini can now proactively text you price-drop alerts, package delivery updates, subscription reminders, and daily briefings. The integration is currently limited to US users and requires Tasks to be enabled in the Gemini app. Google recently made Gemini Tasks available to free users in six countries , including the US, Canada, and India. The company also introduced a feature called Channels , which lets you communicate with Gemini via text messages and email instead of opening the Gemini app every time you need something. Now, that experience is making its way to Google Messages .

articles.title: Yes, There Was One Thing Cut from GTA 6 for Australia, NZ
articles.excerpt: Rockstar chopped out a temporary stat buff from GTA 6, although players down under may not ever really notice it.
articles.body: The Australian version of Grand Theft Auto 6 does differ from the international version in one small way; players down under are not able to use cocaine from their personal inventory to briefly overpower their stamina bar. NZ reportedly has the same version. In GTA 6, baggies of cocaine can be collected (or skimmed from full bricks) and show up as a consumable on the item wheel in the same section as cigarettes, cigars, and joints. Using one triggers a buff that puts stamina in an overpowered state, albeit only for about 30 seconds. This function was never included in the Australian-specific version of the game, as it would have prevented GTA 6 from being classified in the country until it was removed.

articles.excerpt: SpaceX launched its fifth classified mission for U.S. national security this month today (Nov. 24), from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California.
articles.body: SpaceX launched another classified mission for the U.S. Space Force (USSF) today (Nov. 24), sending an unknown payload toward orbit from California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base's Space Launch Complex-4E at TK11:08 a.m. ET (1508 GMT) , carrying the U.S. Space Force's USSF-266 mission. It was the fourth mission SpaceX has launched for the military branch this month. While details about the mission's payload weren't disclosed, it's the fifth space launch in support of U.S. national security in the last two weeks, and comes amid efforts by the Space Force to expand its communications and tracking capabilities.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 24, 1947: The US Navy launches the 1st Aerobee sounding rocket, but it didn't reach space
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 24, 1947, the U.S. Navy launched the first Aerobee rocket into the sky, but it never reached space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 24, 1947, the U.S. Navy launched the first Aerobee rocket into the sky, but it never reached space. Aerobee was a suborbital sounding rocket designed to study Earth's atmosphere . After World War 2, the United States started reusing erman V-2 rockets for this kind of research. When they started running out of V-2 rockets , the United States constructed its own rockets that were similar but cheaper to build and to launch. In the weeks leading up to the first Aerobee mission, three test flights were launched. Those tests used a dummy version of Aerobee with a live booster to see if the two stages would separate properly. On Aerobee's first real flight, the rocket flew about 35 miles high. That's below the 62-mile (100 kilometers) upper limit for the boundary of space .
